name: Gate outcomes by week and vertical
description: What each quality gate passed, rejected or held, broken down by the kind of store. The weekly calibration review is this chart; changing a threshold because of it is a code change that goes through the eval suite, never a click here.

name: Judge fail rate
description: The share of graded drafts the final quality gate refused each day, counting anything but a pass as a refusal, as our own brake does. A sustained rise usually means a prompt or model changed under us, not that the writing got worse.

name: Gate outcomes by rules version
description: Every decision is stamped with the hash of the threshold file that made it, so the effect of changing a number is visible as a break in this chart rather than as a rumour.

name: Calibration report
description: Whether the quality bar is set where we think it is: gate outcomes by week and vertical, the judge's fail rate, and the same broken down by which version of the thresholds decided.

name: Judge fail rate over its ceiling
description: More than 60% of a completed day's graded drafts refused — the ceiling that pauses all generation. Telemetry only: the pause comes from our own counters, and it will not always agree with this. Our code judges the last 50 drafts whenever they happened; this judges whole days. A quiet day with a few refusals can fire here while the code holds off for lack of drafts, and a bad run spread across midnight can pause generation without firing here. It checks only finished days, because a day three drafts old is all noise.
